newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Work to begin at Jewish settlement in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Work to begin at Jewish settlement in Jerusalem.

text.p: Israel was set to begin work on Tuesday on a Jewish neighbourhood in mostly Arab East Jerusalem that has angered Palestinians and drawn worldwide criticism.
"The surveyors will start working on Har Homa on Tuesday," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's communications director David Bar-Illan told Reuters.
Israeli and Palestinian officials were trying to arrange a summit to defuse tensions surrounding Israel's decision to begin building 6,500 housing units for Jews at the disputed hilltop.
Asked about a meeting between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, Bar-Illan said late on Monday:
"There were efforts to arrange a meeting tonight between Prime Minister Netanyahu and Arafat. These efforts will continue to arrange a meeting within the next few days."

The Israeli army declared the area, called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic, a closed military zone. It forbade Israelis from entering and asked Palestinians who had pitched tents at the site in protest to leave.
Israel said on Monday it had reinforced its troops in the West Bank and Gaza Strip to pre-empt any Palestinian violence when ground is broken this week on the project.
"Our working assumption is that incidents are likely to occur, even severe incidents," Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said.
Israel's decision to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in East Jerusalem plunged Arab-Israeli ties to their lowest point since the 1993 PLO-Israeli peace accord and angered Western states.
But the U.S. State Department said on Monday that it believed the Middle East peace process could survive the planned ground-breaking at the site.
"It can survive the groundbreaking," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said, referring to the peace process. He stressed that the United States still did not support the project.

Arafat said on Monday Israel's decision to build was a "flagrant violation to what has been agreed upon". The PLO's official in charge of Jerusalem affairs was more direct. "If they enter with their bulldozers, we will enter," he said.
Palestinians see East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state. Israel views all of Jerusalem as its "eternal" capital.

Under the 1993 PLO-Israel peace accord the future of Jerusalem and the fate of Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza will be determined in 'final status' talks that were supposed to have resumed on Monday.
